newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 27.

text.p: ACC chief sacked after inquiry: Outspoken ACC chief executive Gavin Robins has been sacked after an internal inquiry revealing "unsatisfactory aspects of his performance". Page 1.

Bolger invites ministers to Antarctic meeting: Prime Minister Jim Bolger has invited ministers from other Antarctic Treaty countries to a meeting on Ross Island in New Zealand's Antarctic territory to celebrate the treaty's 40th anniversary. Page 2.

Henare positive about ties with France: Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare said on Monday that he would never forgive France for nuclear testing at Mururoa but was positive about a thawing in relations between France and New Zealand. Page 2.

GPG sells Colonial Motor stake: Malaysian listed car company MBM Resources and associated company Central Shore will buy Guinness Peat Group's 33.9 percent controlling holding in Colonial Motor Company for $27.27 million. Page 13.

Upton warns of Antarctic threat: Antarctica could be seriously damaged unless environmental issues are positively addressed, the Associate Minister of Foreign Affairs, Simon Upton, warned on Monday. Page 1.

Philips sparks phone shake-up: The GSM cellphone market in New Zealand is about to experience a shake-up with the release by newcomer Philips of two phone models, with a third due to be launched in July. Page 28.
Macraes scotches mine rumours: Rumours the Macraes Mining Company was considering closing its Macraes gold mine in Otago have been quashed by managing director Patrick O'Connor. Page 29.
Blue Star gathers more of McCollam: Blue Star mopped up more shares in McCollam Printers on Monday as negotiations with McCollam family continued.
One of Auckland's oldest boutique breweries, Newhegin Breweries Ltd, now in the hands of a liquidator, may be bought by Lion Nathan Breweries.
